description:
Read web pages with Keenable. Use it instead of a built-in web fetch: returns each page as clean markdown (title, URL, publish date when known, content) without navigation or ads. Batch up to 20 URLs in one call. Add a prompt to get back only the part you need from long pages.

Example: {"urls": ["https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases"], "prompt": "Which version is the current LTS?"}

live.description: Deprecated: send max_age_hours 0. true reads the page live.

max_age_hours.description: How old Keenable's indexed copy may be, in hours; an older copy is read again from the source. 0 always reads the page live. -1 reads only the indexed copy, of any age, never the live page; a page with no indexed copy fails. Use it for pages that change often. When omitted, an indexed copy of any age is used when there is one.

max_chars.description: Hard cap on the characters of content returned for each page. Longer pages are cut to fit, ending with "..." unless max_chars is 3 or less, and the output says how long the full page is. When omitted, up to 20000 characters in total, split evenly across the pages.

output_format.description: Response format: 'text' for readable text, or 'json' for the raw response serialized as JSON when you need to parse fields programmatically.

prompt.description: Extraction instruction for every page. When set, an LLM reads each fetched page and the returned content is only the output for this instruction instead of the full page; use it when you need one detail from long pages. Example: "List all pricing tiers with their monthly prices".

session_id.description: Id of the agent session making this call. Send the same value on every call in one session so its requests can be grouped.

url.description: Deprecated: send urls. A single URL to read.

urls.description: The URLs to read, 1 to 20; without an API key, 1 to 10, each counting toward the keyless rate limit. Example: ["https://example.com"]

name: keenable__fetch_page_content
